html:
A massacre in the national stadium of Conakry on 28 September 2009, when soldiers fired on a rally against the military ruler Moussa Dadis Camara, killing more than 150 people.

Soldiers also raped scores of women in the stadium and in the days after. A UN inquiry called it a crime against humanity. Weeks later an aide shot Dadis Camara in the head, he left the country, and a transition led to the 2010 election won by Alpha Conde. A trial of Dadis Camara and others opened in Conakry in 2022, on the anniversary, and in 2024 he was convicted of crimes against humanity, a rare case in Africa of a former ruler tried at home. See also Lansana Conte.
sum: A massacre in the national stadium of Conakry on 28 September 2009, when soldiers fired on a rally against the military ruler Moussa Dadis Camara, killing more than 150 people.
